Heard on I.A. No.25931/2024, which is third application filed under Section 430(1) of B.N.S.S. for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail to appellant Champalal Bhilala.

Appellant stands convicted vide judgment dated 18/08/2022 passed by 18th ASJ and Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012), Bhopal District Bhopal in Special Case No.159/2021 for the offences punishable under Section 376(3) read with section 109 r/w section 16/17 of the POCSO Act, section 366-A and 363 r/w section 109 IPC and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for twenty years along with fine of Rs.1,000/-, R.I. for ten years along with fine of Rs.1,000/-
and R.I. for seven years along with fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively with default stipulation.

sentences.text: Earlier two applications were dismissed as withdrawn by this Court.

Prosecution case in short, which found to be proved is that on 14.8.2020 at about 9 PM the appellant assisted co-accused Rakesh Lohar in kidnapping the prosecutrix from the lawful guardianship of her parents.
In furtherance thereto the appellant also assisted co-accused Rakesh Lohar in committing rape with her.
The prosecutrix was minor at the time of 2 CRA-9678-2022 incident.
On the report of father of the prosecutrix, Crime has been registered, matter was investigated and charge-sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the prosecutrix left her house on her own will and the appellant did not force or compel or induce her to leave her house.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix and co- accused Rakesh have affair, however, the appellant was unknown with the intention of co-accused Rakesh.
The only allegation against the appellant is that he took the prosecutrix to his house on his own motorcycle.
The prosecutrix neither raise any alarm nor made any complain to anybody which shows that she is a consenting party.

sentences.text: The prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
It is also submitted that the appellant has suffered more than two and half years custodial sentence and there is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
Under these circumstances, learned counsel for the appellant prays for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application by contending that looking to the gravity of offence and the role of the appellant in commission of the offence, no case is made out for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the role attributed to the appellant coupled with the fact that the prosecutrix did not raise any alarm when appellant eloped her indicates that she was a 3 CRA-9678-2022 consenting party, in the considered opinion of this Court till disposal of this appeal, execution of jail sentence awarded to the appellant under the impugned judgment deserves to be suspended.

Therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, I.A.
No.25931/2024 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the custodial sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the trial Court concerned on 27/01/2025 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
Accordingly, the aforesaid application stands allowed and disposed of.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
